
---
title: "K–12 Cybersecurity and Data Privacy Research Analysis"
output: html_notebook
---

## Project Overview

This notebook provides an exploratory analysis of survey data related to technology training, educator technology confidence, and cybersecurity and data privacy preparedness in K–12 education.

The analysis uses preliminary survey data to identify potential relationships among these factors and support the development of a practical K–12 Cyber Safety Framework.

Because the dataset is exploratory and limited in size, the findings are used to identify patterns and guide future research rather than establish causal or nationally representative conclusions.

## 1. Load Required Packages

Install the following packages once in your R console if they are not already installed:

`install.packages(c("readxl", "dplyr", "ggplot2"))`

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## 2. Import Survey Data

The spreadsheet should be saved in the same folder as this R Markdown notebook.

```{r import-data}
data <- read_excel(
  "Educator-Technology-and-Training-Survey.xlsx"
)

# Display the first six rows
head(data)

# Display column names
names(data)

# Examine the dataset structure
str(data)
```

## 3. Validate Required Columns

```{r validate-columns}
required_columns <- c(
  "Last Training",
  "Preparedness",
  "Cybersecurity Training",
  "Troubleshooting Confidence",
  "Training Frequency"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(data)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    "The spreadsheet is missing these columns: ",
    paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

cat("All required survey columns are available.\n")
```

## 4. Explore the Dataset

```{r dataset-overview}
# Number of respondents
nrow(data)

# Number of variables
ncol(data)

# Summary statistics
summary(data)

# Missing responses by column
colSums(is.na(data))
```

## 5. Frequency Tables

```{r frequency-tables}
lapply(
  data,
  table,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
```

## 6. Technology Training History

This chart shows when respondents last received technology training.

```{r last-training-chart}
ggplot(
  data,
  aes(x = `Last Training`)
) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "When Teachers Last Received Technology Training",
    x = "Time Since Last Training",
    y = "Number of Respondents"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )
```

## 10. Cybersecurity Training by Training Frequency

This table examines cybersecurity training responses across reported training-frequency categories.

```{r cybersecurity-by-frequency}
cybersecurity_training_frequency <- data %>%
  count(
    `Training Frequency`,
    `Cybersecurity Training`
  ) %>%
  group_by(`Training Frequency`) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(
      n / sum(n) * 100,
      1
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

cybersecurity_training_frequency
```

## 11. Survey Response Summaries

These tables show response counts and percentages for selected survey questions.

```{r survey-summaries}
training_summary <- data %>%
  count(`Training Frequency`) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)
  )

preparedness_summary <- data %>%
  count(`Preparedness`) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)
  )

cybersecurity_summary <- data %>%
  count(`Cybersecurity Training`) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)
  )

confidence_summary <- data %>%
  count(`Troubleshooting Confidence`) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)
  )

training_summary
preparedness_summary
cybersecurity_summary
confidence_summary
```

## 13. Training Frequency and Preparedness

This chart compares reported training frequency with educator preparedness.

It is intended for exploratory analysis and does not establish causation.

```{r training-preparedness-chart}
ggplot(
  data,
  aes(
    x = `Training Frequency`,
    fill = `Preparedness`
  )
) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Training Frequency and Preparedness",
    subtitle = "Exploratory comparison of training frequency and reported preparedness",
    x = "Training Frequency",
    y = "Number of Respondents",
    fill = "Preparedness"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )
```

## 14. Research Limitations

This analysis uses preliminary survey responses from a limited group of educators.

The findings should be interpreted cautiously because:

- The sample may not represent the broader K–12 educator population.
- Responses are self-reported.
- Survey results may be influenced by differences in respondents' roles, experience, and school environments.
- Descriptive comparisons cannot establish causal relationships.

The findings are intended to inform framework development and identify questions for further research.

## 15. Connection to the K–12 Cyber Safety Framework

The exploratory analysis supports the development of a K–12 Cyber Safety Framework by examining educators' reported training experiences, preparedness, cybersecurity training exposure, and technology confidence.

These findings can help identify areas for further investigation and guide the development of practical cybersecurity education resources.

Future work will include refining the framework, improving the Tech Check assessment prototype, and evaluating the usefulness of cybersecurity-readiness indicators.
